episodes.197346: A weakening line of showers and thunderstorms along a cold front pushed southeast through north Alabama during the late morning and midday hours.  A gust front produced winds of 35 to 50 mph which knocked down a couple of trees.
episodes.197390: Under mid-level ridging, seasonably warm and moist air was pooled over Southeast Florida, with a low-level trough sparking numerous slow-moving showers and thunderstorms across the East Coast metro.
episodes.197498: A deep, positively tilted trough moved through the Deep South towards the Southeast. An associated cold front and line of convection moved into the region, but dissipated once it encountered the Appalachians. Ahead of this front and convection, there was sufficient warm air and moisture advection to trigger some isolated thunderstorms along some weak surface convergence. One of these storms developed into a supercell that produced severe hail near Saluda.
episodes.197526: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms developed across eastern Oklahoma during the evening of the 17th, ahead of an approaching cold front. The strongest storms produced severe wind gusts.
episodes.197665: The passage of a warm frontal boundary and mature surface low facilitated high winds along the coast into the coast range. This aforementioned frontal boundary also brought a rise in snow levels increasing river levels, especially those following out of the Willapa Hills where localized river flooding was present.
episodes.198224: As a strong storm system approached, two lines of thunderstorms moved eastward through west Kentucky late on the 17th and early on the 18th. Torrential rainfall from the second line of storms produced some street flooding in Madisonville around 4 AM CST on the 18th. Previously, that line of storms produced estimated wind gusts up to 55 mph in Mayfield at 312 AM CST. The two rounds of thunderstorms, combined with heavy rainfall from the previous few days, helped to produce minor flooding of agricultural areas along the Green River near Paradise. The flooding began in the evening of the 18th and came to an end on the afternoon of the 22nd.
episodes.198315: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front. One storm moved across Calhoun County with quarter size hail.
episodes.198555: Heavy rain led to river flooding at the site of Black Rock from mid into late December.

events.narrative: The ASOS at the McAlester Regional Airport measured 59 mph thunderstorm wind gusts.
Along the Grays river an Emergency manager reported numerous road closures due to high water including Covered Bridge Road, Loop Road, and Altoona-Pillar Rock Road as of the morning of 12-18-2024.
Flooding was reported on McCoy Street, as brief torrential rainfall occurred with a fast-moving line of thunderstorms.

The public reported street flooding with water up to 6 inches deep in the road near State US 1 and E Atlantic Boulevard in Pompano Beach after slow-moving showers and embedded thunderstorms stalled over the area. Rainfall totals were estimated to be around 4 to 6 inches in less than 2 hours.

A member of broadcast media reported street flooding in Oakland Park due to repeated rounds of heavy rain, with at least one car stalled out in the street. Rainfall estimates in the area were 4 to 6 inches in under 2 hours.

The public reported street flooding near Melrose Park after slow-moving showers and embedded thunderstorms stalled over the area. Rainfall totals were estimated to be around 5 to 6 inches in less than 2 hours.
A tree was knocked down at the intersection of George Wallace Highway and Lakeview Lane. Time estimated by radar.
A tree was knocked down at the 3600 block of CR 88 in Pisgah. Time estimated by radar.

River flooding occurred on the Black River at Black Rock from mid to late December with the crest of the river at this site reaching 16.60 feet on December 19th at 0630. The rive flooding at this site would remain in minor flood stage.
